clue.text: Pop showing promise

definitions.meaning: to pop something is to pawn it, handing it over as security

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' is British slang for pawning goods, which is also leaving a pledge; 'showing' just links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Pawning an item means depositing it as security, and a vow is also given as a solemn word of honour.

clue.text: A fixing to hold up creeper

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding something up lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a nail is something used for fixing

explanation.surface: Someone uses a single fastener to support a climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold up' turns A NAIL so it reads upwards, giving the climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical climbing vine with woody stems hanging from forest trees is a kind of creeper.

clue.text: An address so crude is deplorable

indicators.note: something deplorable is in a bad state, so the letters before it are put in disorder

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a coarse speech as shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deplorable' rearranges SO CRUDE IS; 'is' does double duty only in the surface, as it is fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal speech or lecture delivered to an audience is a discourse.

clue.text: Pass — but would fail without superior English

indicators.note: in a down clue, superior means placed above, so English sits on top of the other piece

parts.note: to lapse is to fail or fall away

explanation.surface: A student passes, but would have failed without top marks in English.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the E placed on top and the answer 'would fail', becoming LAPSE; 'without' gives that reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to go by or slip away, which is to pass.

clue.text: Brainy brother tucked into breakfast food

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another, as food is tucked into

parts.note: cereal is a typical breakfast food

explanation.surface: A clever sibling is eating his cornflakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests eating, but it puts BR inside CEREAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebral describes someone intellectual, using the brain rather than feelings.

clue.text: Fantastic constructions by rooks on the wing

parts.note: a rook in chess is also called a castle
a bird on the wing is flying, up aloft

explanation.surface: Rooks, the birds, are flying near some imaginative buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: The rooks look like birds, which 'on the wing' supports, but they are chess pieces, also called castles.
explanation.definitionFit: Daydreams and impractical schemes are fanciful structures with no foundation.

clue.text: Set up hospital division away from the front

parts.note: to rear is to raise or set up
a ward is a section of a hospital

explanation.surface: Someone establishes a hospital department well behind the battle lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving towards the back, away from the front, is the sense of backward motion.

clue.text: At first, buffet host offers bananas, nuts or crackers

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word buffet is used

parts.note: a host is a great multitude, an army

explanation.surface: A party host serves fruit, nuts and savoury biscuits at a buffet.
explanation.walkthrough: The food words make up the definition: bananas, nuts and crackers are all slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: All three slang words describe someone crazy or mad.

clue.text: Non-participant disturbs set in a bar

indicators.note: disturbing letters moves them out of order, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who refuses to join in disrupts a group in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbs' rearranges SET IN A BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who declines to vote or take part abstains from it.

clue.text: Old Nick's main following group

indicators.note: the word main comes after group, so its letters go second

parts.note: to marshal is to group or arrange
the main is a poetic word for the sea

explanation.surface: The devil's chief disciples form a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Nick' looks like the devil but means an old prison, nick being British slang for jail; the Marshalsea was a notorious London debtors' prison.
explanation.definitionFit: This former Southwark jail, a lockup for debtors, has long since closed.

clue.text: Right to employ stratagem

parts.note: to employ is to use

explanation.surface: Someone claims the right to use a clever plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A trick or scheme intended to deceive is a stratagem.

clue.text: Cold awakening after drinking party

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
arousal is a waking or stirring up

explanation.surface: Waking up feeling cold after a night of boozing at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy session of heavy drinking and merrymaking is a revel.

clue.text: Amateur on the road causing hold up

indicators.note: in an across clue, one word on another follows it, so amateur comes after road

parts.note: a way is a road
lay means non-professional or amateur

explanation.surface: An inexperienced driver on the road causes a traffic jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold up' reads as a traffic delay but is the verb to ambush.
explanation.definitionFit: To ambush or stop someone, such as a traveller, is to hold them up.

clue.text: Just beautiful

definitions.meaning: lovely, as in an old poetic sense

explanation.definitionFit: Equitable treatment and old-fashioned loveliness are both senses of the one adjective.

clue.text: Accommodation in suitable environment for painters

indicators.note: an environment surrounds something, so suitable is wrapped round painters

parts.note: apt means suitable
painters are art men

explanation.surface: Housing set in surroundings that suit artists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'environment for' puts ART MEN inside APT.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat or set of rooms to live in is a form of lodging.

clue.text: Directed to collect soil taken back from grating

indicators.note: collecting something takes it inside, so directed holds the other piece

parts.note: sent means directed or dispatched

indicators.note: taken back means the word for soil is read backwards

parts.note: dirt is soil

explanation.surface: Someone was told to gather earth from a drain cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken back' reverses DIRT to TRID, and 'to collect' puts it inside SENT. 'grating' looks like a metal grille but is the adjective harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh, loud and unpleasant noise is jarring.

clue.text: Doctor sends out notes about directions for treatment

definitions.note: the definition is a singular noun; the answer is plural, the bandages applied in treatment

indicators.note: about means around, so the doctor and singing pieces surround the directions

parts.note: someone who sings sends out musical notes
E and S are compass directions, east and south

explanation.surface: A doctor issues written instructions about how to treat a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' look like written messages but are musical: one who sings sends them out. 'about' places ES between DR and SINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandages and sterile pads applied to wounds are used in medical care.

clue.text: Pushing off cruel revolutionary

indicators.note: something revolutionary overturns the order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cruel revolutionary is being pushed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges OFF CRUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing describes someone assertive and vigorous.

clue.text: Oarsman returns in vessel showing stress

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the vessel

parts.note: a can is a vessel

indicators.note: returns means the word for oarsman is read backwards

parts.note: an oarsman is a rower

explanation.surface: A rower returning in a boat looks exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses ROWER to REWOR, which goes 'in' CAN; the vessel looks like a boat but is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A face lined and tired from worry and anxiety shows strain.

clue.text: Colour for City footballers

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
RU is Rugby Union, played by footballers of that code

explanation.surface: A football club's kit colour for Manchester City or another team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' looks like a football club, but it is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is a pale greyish-yellow shade, like unbleached linen.

clue.text: Excluded from Shakespeare in a recital

indicators.note: a recital is spoken out to an audience, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: Shakespeare is known as the Bard

explanation.surface: Someone was left out of a Shakespeare performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a recital' signals a sound-alike: BARD said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Being barred means being banned or shut out.

clue.text: Spoiling the reception by not circulating?

definitions.meaning: radio interference crackling and ruining what is received

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both crackling interference on the radio and motionless.

clue.text: Subject of Crown in charge

parts.note: the crown of a head or hill is its top

explanation.surface: A subject of the Crown is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' looks like a royal subject, but it is a theme; Crown is the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme or matter under discussion is the subject.

clue.text: Ko-ko, perhaps, .had means for capital adjustment

indicators.note: an adjustment alters arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Mikado's executioner had a method for capital punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Ko-Ko is the Lord High Executioner in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado. 'adjustment' rearranges HAD MEANS; 'capital' hints at beheading.
explanation.definitionFit: Ko-Ko is an example of an executioner who beheads people with an axe.

clue.text: Give leave in naval lower deck

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words naval lower

explanation.surface: Leave is granted on the sailors' lower deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the run inside 'naval lower'.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit or let someone do something is to give them leave.

clue.text: Harvest pear damaged

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so the letters of pear are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fruit crop has been spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges PEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather in a crop is to harvest it.

clue.text: Openly and unhesitatingly embracing relative

indicators.note: embracing holds something inside, so unhesitatingly wraps round the relative

parts.note: to refuse flatly is to refuse outright, unhesitatingly
gran, grandmother, is a relative

explanation.surface: Someone openly and readily hugs a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' puts GRAN inside FLATLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something flagrantly means doing it blatantly, in plain view.

clue.text: Student labelled a pedant

annotationWithheld.why: Student labelled a pedant (8): STICKLER needs L inside STICKER, but 'labelled' would have to supply STICKER and also signal the containment, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Reject grant by underworld boss

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
to own is to grant or admit

explanation.surface: A gangland leader refuses a grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld boss' looks like a gangster, but it is Dis, the Roman god of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to repudiate or cut them off.
